summary.intent: Investigate GitHub issue #644 (hardware verification gates for the crates/fuse FUSE-T/FSKit driver decision) and run the required pre-implementation gates 1–5 to de-risk the driver choice.
summary.outcome: Upgraded FUSE-T to 1.2.7, built a hw-gates test harness, and ran gates 1–4: gate 1 passes only with the noattrcache mount option (default mount has unbounded staleness), gates 2 and 3 pass outright, gate 4 found commercial bundling requires a paid license, gate 5 is blocked on lacking macOS 27 beta hardware. Results and blueprint updates were committed after resolving a 1Password SSH-signing delay.

repo: FUSE-T default mount has smbfs pin attributes to a 3s cache that ignores FUSE reply TTLs, and inval_inode never reaches already-cached data pages (staleness unbounded, >300s observed)
Mounting with the `noattrcache` option fixes coherence: 0.3-5ms p95 attr/data invalidation latency with no throughput cost (~1GB/s cold, ~6GB/s warm)
crates/fuse must mount with noattrcache and the sync engine must fire invalidation on every remote change — recorded in blueprint/desktop.md
FUSE-T's smbfs client does a `.smbdelete` rename shuffle internally under overwrite-rename; v1's 8-byte name-truncation bug did not reproduce on 1.2.7
FUSE-T 1.2.7 now ships two pkgs: org.fuse-t.core and org.fuse-t.fskit (an FSKit backend), but that FSKit backend doesn't support notifications so it isn't a shortcut for gate 5

macFUSE and FUSE-T both register as `fuse` in pkg-config, so an unpinned build can silently link the wrong libfuse and trigger macFUSE's kext approval prompt — must use otool -L to verify the linked library and/or pin fuse-t.pc explicitly

The patched/vendored fuser source used for v1 lives only on the frozen `v1` branch (not in current vendor dir, which only had a leftover Cargo.lock) — must be extracted from `v1` branch when needed on v2
libfuse-t exports fuse_mount_compat25, so linking should use the plain libfuse2 path, not macfuse-4-compat

code.finding: Patched to prefer fuse-t.pc over generic fuse.pc so the harness links libfuse-t.dylib instead of macFUSE's libfuse, avoiding accidental kext-load prompts
Location of the sync-timing-profile constants that gate 1 results were meant to update; ultimately no kernel TTL constants were needed since noattrcache + push invalidation replace them

workflow: When a background/long-running command's binary hasn't been verified, check linked libraries (otool -L) before executing anything that touches kernel extensions or system-level mount hooks
When a user sends a message mid-turn (including during a blocking dialog like a kext prompt), stop and answer immediately rather than continuing tool calls and burying the response
Background task results should be checked via the returned output-file path once a task-notification with status completed arrives, rather than polling

friction: A build accidentally linked macFUSE's libfuse instead of FUSE-T's, triggering an unexpected macOS kernel-extension approval dialog on the user's machine

The assistant continued working through two subsequent user messages instead of immediately addressing the alarming kext prompt, causing user frustration ('the actual fuck') that was explicitly about being ignored, not the technical issue itself
Vendored fuser source in the current branch was stale/incomplete (just a Cargo.lock), requiring extraction from the frozen v1 branch
1Password SSH commit signing failed to prompt/respond, blocking the final commit until the user returned from being away (afk)
Extended gate 1 runs took a long time (held-open-fd rounds hit 10s/30s timeouts) and had to be moved to background execution
open_items: Gate 5 (FSKit spike) remains blocked on hardware — needs a macOS 27 beta machine or VM to test FSVolume.DataCacheHandler and FSClient.mountSingleVolume
Gate 4 license conditional — needs actual commercial license negotiation with FUSE-T author (alex@fuse-t.org) before bundling FUSE-T in the shipped app
Debug SMB mount and background serve process needed manual teardown mid-session; confirm no other stray hw-gates mounts/processes remain
PR for the #644 work still needs to be opened and run through mandatory /simplify and /security-review gates after the commit lands
